title: How do you shrink a war's casualty count? Give it a new webpage.
body: The Intercept reports the Pentagon has quietly changed how it tallies dead and wounded from the Iran war. Casualties since July 7 now live on a separate webpage under a bland label, "Overseas Operations." A U.S. government official told The Intercept the new method was "designed to obscure the count." The numbers are the tell. That page alone lists 273 troops killed or wounded since July 7. Add the older Iran war page and the official count hits 704, an 83 percent jump since the April 8 ceasefire. Count the casualties the system left out and the real total tops 900.

Watch the older page and it moves the wrong way. On July 21 the count for Operation Epic Fury, the military's official name for the war, stood at 500. Now it reads 431. Casualties went down on paper while Iranian attacks went up. The Pentagon told the New York Times this is just bookkeeping, that finished operations get filed under CENTCOM. The official was blunter. "This is certainly designed to conceal the count of the wounded."

Trump and Hegseth spent months insisting Iran's military was annihilated. Then Iran hit at least nine U.S. outposts and overwhelmed American air defenses. When you have to split the casualties across two webpages to keep the number low, you are not winning the war. You are managing the story about it.
